articles.title: Bitter and sweet: on FSSAI draft restrictions, added sugars in infant foods
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Food Safety and Standards Regulations 2020 currently allow manufacturers to add sucrose and fructose, provided their combined total does not exceed 20% of the carbohydrates in a product intended for infants aged 0-6 months. In a draft proposal, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has pitched to eliminate this allowance — in line with WHO’s recommendation to have infants breastfeed exclusively for the first six months, followed by nutritionally adequate complementary foods avoiding added sugars until 24 months. While corporations have defended sugary formulations as abiding by the Codex Alimentarius, public health experts have repeatedly described their decision to sell infant foods with added sugar as nutritional dumping. Adding sugar has often been a commercial strategy, as it serves as a cheap bulking agent, improves palatability and encourages repeat purchases. WHO’s nutrient and promotion profile model for baby foods in 2022 also identified sweet purées and products in which fruits released sugars during processing as concerns. While the FSSAI’s draft proposal is a step in the right direction, stopping here would allow manufacturers to replace sucrose with another sweetening ingredient. It should assess the ingredients that manufacturers add and the nutritional profile of the finished food, thus completing the loop, with the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles, and Infant Foods Act 1992 rightly restricting aggressively the marketing of infant foods for children up to two years old.

Research has found that children who regularly received sweetened water during infancy subsequently preferred sweeter liquids, while exposure to different infant formula flavours influenced their dietary preferences years later, including for foods tasting neutral or bitter. Across both personal and public health dimensions, then, infants need to encounter diverse flavours. Since the 2024 dietary guidelines of the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition say that children under two should avoid added sugars, the FSSAI’s draft proposal limiting itself to six months seems like a concession to manufacturers. This should be avoided since India’s regulatory response to ultra-processed foods is expanding after years of sluggishness. India is currently mulling restrictions on added sugar in foods for the youngest infants, on unhealthy foods around schools, and on front-of-pack labelling for packaged foods. If the FSSAI does not expand its proposed restriction to cover all added sugars and extend it across the first 24 months, and pair it with mandatory, interpretative front-of-pack labelling for all foods, its regulatory progress will remain incomplete.

articles.title: England's Bodhana Sivanandan becomes International Master at age of 11, breaks 38-year-old record
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indian-origin English chess player Bodhana Sivanandan has become the youngest female International Master (IM) at the age of 11, breaking a 38-year-old record set by Judit Polgar.

Sivanandan, who hails from Harrow in north London, needed only a few rating points to qualify for the open IM title and break Polgar's record, while also securing a place among the 10 youngest IMs of all time.
"Congratulations to 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan on becoming an International Master with a final-round win at the European Women's Chess Club Cup 2026!" the European Chess Union wrote on X.
"Bodhana delivered a fantastic performance, scoring 5.5/7 on Board 1 for She Plays to Win Lionesses, making her the youngest female player in history to earn the IM title," it added.

At this week's European Women's Chess Club Cup, Sivanandan came close to drawing her opening-round match against Russian Grandmaster Aleksandra Goryachkina before defeating Belarusian International Master Olga Badelka in the third round to take her rating to 2399.4.
She then drew against Georgian Grandmaster Nino Batsiashvili in the following round.
However, her 32-move victory over Sweden's Woman International Master Viktoria Johansson helped her achieve the distinction and join the list of the 10 youngest IMs of all time.
The list includes India's R. Praggnanandhaa and D. Gukesh, Uzbekistan's Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Argentina's Faustino Oro, Turkey's Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus and Russia's Roman Shogdzhiev.

articles.title: El Nino-induced water and power crisis likely to persist until July 2027: Telangana CM Revanth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy warned that Telangana could face prolonged drinking water crisis until July next year due to the impact of El Nino, affecting agricultural operations and increased electricity consumption.

Addressing a high-level meeting on the State’s preparedness to tackle El Nino-related conditions on Friday, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the government had been alerting people about the impending situation for the last six months, but political opponents were now accusing the Congress government of “bringing drought to Telangana”.

El Nino is not confined to Telangana, but affecting countries such as England and the United States and even States like Maharashtra, where some regions had already introduced water rationing , he added.

The Chief Minister said the State could witness a further deterioration in drinking water availability as temperatures rose and reservoirs and irrigation projects had limited water stocks. There is not even 200 tmc feet in reservoirs, and people should adapt to the situation as they did during the pandemic. High temperatures in summer will prevail, he said, warning people to be cautious. He said that out of 30 lakh pump sets, 15 lakh have already dried up.

He stressed that public representatives and officials should not conceal the severity of the problem. The public should be informed about the challenges and the measures being taken to address them or else they may end up believing in BRS’s propaganda.

The Chief Minister also cautioned that electricity availability was becoming a serious concern. The State was experiencing power demand of 20,000 MW compared to 13,000 MWs recorded in undivided Andhra Pradesh in the same period. He asked consumers to avoid unnecessary consumption of power and water. Government offices, in particular, should adopt measures to conserve power.

The CM also said that the government would make every effort to provide water for the ensuing kharif crop. However, farmers should make informed decisions about sowing, instead of being misled by political statements that could expose them to crop losses in the next season. He appealed to farmers to cultivate only rainfed crops and vegetables in view of the depletion of the water resources.

The CM announced that a special scheme will be introduced after Sankranti for four months until May, to provide daily employment to workers. “We must provide work to every individual and ensure that everyone has food to eat. This scheme must be meticulously designed and implemented. ‘Kalajathas’ (cultural troupes) should be organised to motivate farmers.” He also called for special measures to protect livestock, including adequate fodder and drinking water for animals.
Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, TPCC president Mahesh Kumar Goud, Ministers and MLAs were present.

fullParagraphs: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) has issued four observations to Gland Pharma’s formulation facility near Hyderabad.

The four Form 483 observations followed an unannounced inspection on current good manufacturing practice (cGMP) at the facility in Dundigal between October 12 and 23. The observations are procedural in nature and the corrective and preventive actions will be submitted to the U.S. FDA within the stipulated period.
The observations issued are neither repeat observations nor related to data integrity, the company said in a filing on Friday (October 24, 2026).

articles.title: Haryana gangsters Himanshu Bhau, Neeraj Faridpuria detained in U.S.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Gangsters Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria, wanted in several cases of murder, extortion and high-profile shootings, have been detained by U.S. authorities in Las Vegas following a tip-off from the Haryana Special Task Force (STF).
Confirming the development, Haryana STF Inspector General Simardeep Singh told The Hindu that both gangsters had been detained in Las Vegas.

Himanshu, a native of Ritoli village in Rohtak district, allegedly entered the world of crime at the age of 17, when he was booked in an attempted murder and extortion case, STF sources said. In 2020, he escaped from a juvenile correctional facility in Hisar and subsequently established his gang.

He fled India in 2022 using a fake passport and travelled through Dubai and Portugal before allegedly entering the U.S. illegally about two years ago. He is suspected of remotely directing a network of shooters in India through encrypted messaging applications to carry out extortion and targeted attacks.
A total of 64 criminal cases are registered against him, said the Haryana Police sources.
Neeraj Faridpuria, a native of Palwal district, faces more than two dozen criminal cases registered in Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, involving murder, extortion and organised crime.

The two gangsters had also claimed responsibility for the shooting outside the Gurugram residence of YouTuber Elvish Yadav last year. Shooters allegedly fired 25 to 30 rounds outside the house in an incident linked to extortion and betting promotions.

articles.title: How is Kerala planning to prevent child deaths linked to malnutrition and neglect? Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The story so far: A two-year-old boy died in Alappuzha district’s Karthikapally , near Haripad, on October 18 allegedly owing to severe malnutrition and acute anaemia. The death occurred when the boy’s mother was admitted to Government Medical College Hospital, Vandanam, for giving birth. The boy weighed around 7.5 kg against the average weight of 12 kg for a two-year-old child.

The child’s death shook the State, raising questions about the effectiveness of child protection measures. This was the mother’s seventh delivery. The couple has four other children, all girls, besides the newborn, a boy. Another child, again a boy, had died earlier.

The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a suo motu case in connection with the incident. The district child welfare committee (CWC) has taken over the care of the four girl children.

The Thrikkunnapuzha police who have registered a case of unnatural death are awaiting the results of a histopathology test to confirm whether the child’s death was owing to some illness or malnourishment. The health condition of the surviving children is also being examined, the police said.

According to Women and Child Development (WCD) department and panchayat authorities, the family mostly lived an itinerant life, rarely staying put at one place for long. They mostly lived in rented accommodation, moving away whenever some intervention from the authorities was expected in the wake complaints from the people or the mechanisms under the WCD and the Health departments.
The constant moving also made it difficult for the authorities to monitor them.

The four girl children had been living in a child care institution since December 2024. During the summer vacation this year, the couple insisted that the children return to live with them. The CWC accordingly issued an order. However, the parents refused to send the girl children back to the care home even after the vacation despite repeated pleas.

In June this year, the family was moved to Gandhi Bhavan at Pathanapuram following the intervention of Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala, who is the local MLA, and ASHA and anganwadi workers. The whole family was promised not only accommodation, but work too. However, they did not remain there for even a week, returning after the mother threatened to commit suicide and starve themselves.

On October 6, attempts were made by WCD department officials, panchayat officials, ASHA worker, Health officials, and the police to shift the couple’s children to a care home but were met with stiff resistance from the mother. They had to step back after the mother threatened self-harm and that to the baby.
A decision was then made to shift the children to safety when the mother was admitted to hospital for giving birth. However, the toddler passed away when the mother was hospitalised.
At the time of his death, the family was living in a house at Karthikapally that belonged to the husband’s family. However, it was said to be in a deplorable condition.
WCD officials say food was provided from anganwadis for the mother and younger children and efforts made to enrol the oldest child in school.

articles.title: Election Commission sought explanation from officials as goof-up in voter list went viral
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: After unusual names and details cropped up in the electoral roll for Legislative Council polls in Uttar Pradesh , the Election Commission sought an explanation from the concerned Electoral Registration Officer, who is the Divisional Commissioner and Additional Electoral Registration Officer. The error led to uproar on social media.

Entries such as “Ram ne Yadav ko maara”, “Ram ne Sharma ko maara” as names and “B.Com” in place of a voter’s father’s name have surfaced in the electoral roll for the Legislative Council polls held on Friday (October 23, 2026). The discrepancies were found in the Allahabad graduate constituency voter list ahead of polling.

“For the first time, an online registration facility has been provided in Uttar Pradesh for adding names to the voter list for the Legislative Council elections. There is a possibility of mistakes when doing any work for the first time. Out of 14,81,310 entries in the voter list, there are a total of 158 entries in which the names of the voters or their relatives appear strange. The strangeness of these names is due to such a mistake. The software was supposed to transliterate the names typed in English into Hindi, but probably due to some error, it translated them. For example, when Ram hit Yadav was typed, the software translated it as ‘Ram hit Yadav’. There was a system to edit and correct such mistakes, but where people were not careful, such mistakes persisted. Typing B Com in place of father is a human error or negligence,” reads a statement issued by the Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh.

The statement further reads, “The Divisional Commissioner is the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) in this voter list, and the District Officer of the concerned district is the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO). It is their responsibility to keep the voter list free from all errors. An explanation has been sought from them in this regard. Instructions have been given to the district officers to ensure that voters do not face any problem due to this mistake,”.

The five graduates’ constituencies namely Lucknow, Agra, Meerut, Varanasi and Allahabad-Jhansi, while the six teachers’ constituencies include Lucknow, Agra, Meerut, Varanasi, Bareilly-Moradabad and Gorakhpur-Faizabad covering over 30 districts in U.P. went for polls with over 14 lakh voters.

articles.title: IndusInd Bank posts profit of ₹1,242 crores in Q2; asset quality improvement and interest income drives growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: IndusInd Bank Limited posted a net profit of ₹1,242 crore for the quarter ended September, up 20% sequentially and trimming net loss of ₹437 for the same quarter in the preceding year. The bank had incurred net loss for the same period in previous year due to an increase in microfinance provisioning and write-offs.

The bank’s bottom line for Q2FY27 was supported by a rise in net interest income, which stood at ₹4,569 crore as against ₹4,409 crores a year ago. Sequentially, interest income declined by 2%. NII for half year (H1FY27) rose to ₹9,254, up 2.3% on year.

Asset quality of the bank improved substantially, with gross non-performing assets (NPA) ratio at 2.73% compared to 3.60% on year and net NPA declining to 0.83% from 1.04% in Q2FY26. However, the net interest margin of the bank slipped to 3.23% from 3.32% a year ago.

Net revenue of the bank for the period rose to ₹6,817 crores compared to ₹6,00 crores a year. A decline in operating expenses also helped push the bottom-line numbers, with expenses slipping to ₹3,943 crores in July-Septemeber from ₹4,013 crore for the same period last year.
Deposits of the bank rose 10% year-on-year to ₹4.28 crores. Advances of the bank for the period stood at 3.63 crores.
IndusInd held provisions of $9,012 crore as of September 30, with the provision coverage ratio at 70%.

IndusInd Bank raised nearly $3.5 billion via the Reserve Bank of India’s special window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) account, which was impacted the contraction in NIM. The bank said recovery in margin related to FCNR-B is expected over the next two quarters.

“Q2 reflects the growing strength of the IndusInd Bank franchise and the progress we have made in rebuilding momentum across the business. Our Q2 results demonstrate that the growth has strengthened, profitability has improved, asset quality trends remain encouraging, and our funding profile is becoming more granular and resilient,” Rajiv Anand, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of IndusInd Bank said.

The bank also informed the exchanges on Friday (October 23, 2026) that the Board of Directors of the lender has appointed Priyanka Sinha as an Additional Director in the category of Non-Executive Independent Director for a period of four consecutive years, till October 22, 2030.

Speaking to the media at post-earnings conference call, the bank said it remains confident of reaching a 1% exit return on assets for FY27. Bank also expects loans growth momentum to continue driven by retail and wholesale lending. Shares of IndusInd Bank Ltd closed at ₹835.00 on Friday, down 1.76%, on the BSE.

articles.title: Government to modify labour survey to capture gig economy, unpaid household workers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union government has decided to change the design and structure of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) to track digital platform workers and capture engagement in unpaid household, caregiving, volunteer, and trainee work. The PLFS will also include additional questions to measure labour underutilisation.

According to a press release and concept note issued in New Delhi on Friday (October 23, 2026), the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), has proposed modifications to the PLFS sampling design starting January 2027. The survey schedule will also change.
The Ministry has invited comments and suggestions from policymakers, researchers, academic institutions, and the public within 15 days from Friday.

A separate Second Stage Stratum (SSS) will be introduced in the PLFS to identify households with at least one digital platform worker. An additional entry will be added to the questionnaire to determine whether any member of the household has engaged in digital platform work during the specified reference period.

“There will be four SSSs in rural areas and five in urban areas, with 14 households canvassed in each selected First Stage Unit (FSU). This revision in SSS formation is expected to improve the coverage of digital platform workers and facilitate more comprehensive data collection on this emerging segment of the labour market,” the press release said.

According to the concept note, a large proportion of women in India spend considerable time on unpaid household and caregiving activities, such as cooking, cleaning, childcare, and caring for elderly, sick, or disabled family members. “While such activities contribute significantly to household well-being and facilitate the participation of other household members in paid employment, they have not been measured separately in PLFS until now,” it noted, adding that specific questions will be incorporated to capture engagement in own-use production of goods, unpaid household and caregiving activities, volunteer work, and unpaid trainee work.

Additionally, the criteria for sample allocation and stratification have been updated based on the experience of the previous two years. “These revisions are expected to improve the efficiency of sample allocation and stratification and ensure better representation of population variations, which in turn will minimise operational difficulties during sample selection,” the press release said.

articles.title: Crude oil sourcing presently volatile; procuring more on landed basis: HPCL Chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Crude oil sourcing at present is very volatile and unpredictable, and Hindustan Petroleum is procuring more on a delivered basis than free-on-board (FOB) and term contracts, Vikas Kaushal, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of the state-owned oil-marketing company told analysts in an investor call on Friday (October 23, 2026).
Purchases on delivered basis entail the seller bearing the cost of shipping the oil and associated risks until it reaches the buyer’s port or facility.

“All I can say if you look at crude premiums and landed cost: there are times when there are premiums and there are times when you can even pick it up at discounts. It is a very ‘Wild West’ right now” he said.
Separately, Mr. Kaushal also explained there could be instances of discount though the freights could be very high at that time.
Srividya Venkataraman, Director (Finance) informed analysts that freight costs had doubled between the first quarter and the second quarter.
She observed that shipping costs on a Suezmax tanker moved up to $9 per barrel from around $4 per barrel in June.
Though, Mr. Kaushal also stated that landed price may not be as high as it may appear.

“The producers of oil are also stuck. Thus, the astronomical freight rates that you see: if you strike a good deal, you can get is almost managed on the producer,” he explained, adding, “So, the net back to producers in many situations, especially those who are stuck or where there is stranded oil right now, the net backs are much lower than what is in the public domain.”

The HPCL chief also told analysts that the company is procuring more on landed basis expect in cases where sending a ship is cheaper. He added this is also to avert the probability of a ship being attacked enroute.
Ms. Venkataraman informed that under-recoveries on liquified petroleum gas (LPG) stood at ₹245 per cylinder in October and is projected at ₹327 per cylinder in November.
She added that the total under-recovery for LPG in the September-end quarter stood at ₹500 crores.

Separately, Mr. Kaushal also informed analysts that Hindustan Petroleum has petrol and diesel stocks combined for twenty days. This excludes the crude that is presently being processed in their refineries.

articles.title: Net FDI at $3.3 billion in September 2026, positive for third consecutive month
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Net foreign direct investment (FDI) remained positive for the third consecutive month in August 2026, with inflows exceeding outflows by $3.3 billion, according to the latest data by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). This was driven by robust inflows even as outward investment by Indian companies fell.

“FDI flows continued to remain robust in August 2026, supported by strong gross inflows and moderation in outward FDI,” the RBI said in its monthly Bulletin. “Communication, miscellaneous services and manufacturing received more than two-thirds of the FDI inflows.”

Net FDI, which is the difference between the total direct investment coming in and the total going out, was positive in seven out of the last eight months. This is a significant turnaround from the five consecutive months of negative net FDI India saw during August-December 2025.

The data shows that gross FDI into India, or the total that entered the country as direct investment, stood at $11.1 billion in August 2026, which was 24% lower than in the previous month, but nearly 68% higher than in August last year.
“The U.S., Singapore and Mauritius were the major source countries, accounting for about 72% of FDI inflows,” the report noted.

Total outflows increased marginally to $7.7 billion in August 2026 as compared to $7.2 billion in July, and $6.7 billion in August 2025. However, in this, the driver was the repatriation by foreign companies operating in India rather than outward investment by Indian companies.

“Outward FDI flows moderated in August with more than half being directed towards Singapore, the Netherlands, and the U.S,” the RBI said. “The major sectors of outward FDI were agriculture & mining, financial, insurance & business services, and manufacturing — together accounting for more than two-thirds of the outward flows.”

Remittances increased to $5.8 billion in August 2026, which was nearly 52% higher than in July, and 28% higher than in August last year. This was largely balanced out by a fall in outward FDI, which fell to $1.9 billion. This was more than 43% lower than in July 2026 and 11% lower than in August last year.
Looking at the longer time-period of April-August 2026, the RBI noted that gross inward FDI and net FDI flows were both higher during this period.

A slowdown in the pace of outward FDI along with sustained higher gross FDI inflows supported net FDI flows,” the RBI said. “Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing accounted for around 73% of total FDI equity inflows during April-August 2026.”

articles.title: Data suggests broad-based increase in food prices: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: High-frequency data collected by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for October (till 19th), suggest a broad-based increase in food prices, said RBI officials in the October edition of RBI Bulletin, which was released on Friday (October 23, 2026).

“Among cereals, rice and wheat prices continued to increase. Prices of major pulses also went up sequentially. Edible oil prices also recorded a slow and broad-based increase, led by mustard and palm oil,” they wrote in the ‘State of the Economy’ article.
Among vegetables, while potato prices declined and the pace of onion price increases dropped, tomato prices picked up, they added.

Surprisingly, inflation in rural areas has been getting higher than that in urban areas. Inflation stood at 4.9% and 6.1%, respectively, in urban and rural areas in September. In August, urban and rural inflation stood at 4.3% and 5.2% respectively, the officials stated.
ALSO WATCH The battle against inflation is entering a tougher phase: What it means for you

The majority of States/UTs recorded inflation in the range of 4-6% in September. Inflation ranged from 2.9% to 6.9% across states/UTs. States like Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry recorded inflation in excess of 6% across both rural and urban areas, they pointed out.

Stating that WPI inflation recorded its first double-digit rate in the new series (Base 2022-23) at 11.4% in September 2026, rising from 9.9% in August, reflecting a broad-based increase in prices, they said industrial and farm input costs remained elevated.
Inflation in the Output Producer Price Index surged to 11.4% in September 2026 from 9.8% in August, led by manufacturing products, and mining & quarrying, they said.
As per the article headline, CPI inflation edged up over the months and showed signs of greater generalisation across commodities, calling for a commensurate change in the monetary policy stance.
“The external headwinds are also being dealt with a slew of regulatory measures by the Reserve Bank to curb speculative activity in foreign exchange market,” they stated.

“Strong inflows under FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) and remittance flows strengthened in August. With strong exports growth, the trade deficit narrowed in September,” they added.

The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5% (YoY) in September from 4.8% in August, driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel and core (CPI excluding food and fuel) components.

articles.title: England's Bodhana Sivanandan becomes International Master at age of 11, breaks 38-year-old record
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Indian-origin English chess player Bodhana Sivanandan has become the youngest female International Master (IM) at the age of 11, breaking a 38-year-old record set by Judit Polgar.

Sivanandan, who hails from Harrow in north London, needed only a few rating points to qualify for the open IM title and break Polgar's record, while also securing a place among the 10 youngest IMs of all time.
"Congratulations to 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan on becoming an International Master with a final-round win at the European Women's Chess Club Cup 2026!" the European Chess Union wrote on X.
"Bodhana delivered a fantastic performance, scoring 5.5/7 on Board 1 for She Plays to Win Lionesses, making her the youngest female player in history to earn the IM title," it added.

At this week's European Women's Chess Club Cup, Sivanandan came close to drawing her opening-round match against Russian Grandmaster Aleksandra Goryachkina before defeating Belarusian International Master Olga Badelka in the third round to take her rating to 2399.4.
She then drew against Georgian Grandmaster Nino Batsiashvili in the following round.
However, her 32-move victory over Sweden's Woman International Master Viktoria Johansson helped her achieve the distinction and join the list of the 10 youngest IMs of all time.
The list includes India's R. Praggnanandhaa and D. Gukesh, Uzbekistan's Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Argentina's Faustino Oro, Turkey's Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus and Russia's Roman Shogdzhiev.

articles.title: France to deploy 70,000 police for fresh weekend protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: France will deploy about 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests on Saturday (October 24, 2026) after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.
Protests by high school students over learning conditions sparked a movement that has since spread nationwide, fuelled by broader anger over the rising cost of living.

About 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 24, 2026), Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a news conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen as the frontrunner and indicating her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is due at the weekend to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected and local authorities fearing clashes as counter-protesters also head to the city south of Paris.

Mr. Macron met representatives of secondary school pupils on Friday (October 23, 2026), but they emerged from the talks urging students to keep protesting until the government put forward concrete proposals to address their demands.
Mr. Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last Saturday.
Courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.
On Thursday (October 22, 2026), Mr. Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.
An extreme-left group in western France posted on its website a call for its supporters to be “uncatchable, unpredictable, to evade the deployment” of police.
Authorities have stepped up security measures and imposed restrictions on protests.
In Orleans, between 20,000 and 30,000 people are expected to come out against Le Pen’s National Rally party, but the gathering will be barred from the city centre, the prefecture said.

articles.title: Preliminary magnitude 6.9 earthquake hits off coast of Vanuatu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A preliminary magnitude 6.9 earthquake on Friday (October 23, 2026) hit off the coast of Vanuatu, according to the U.S. Geological Survey, prompting a tsunami warning for the area that was later rescinded.

The quake in the South Pacific struck at around 1:30 p.m. and was centred 197 kilometres (122 miles) west-northwest of Port-Orly, at a depth of 10 km. Several aftershocks were later recorded in the area, including a preliminary magnitude 6.3 quake, according to the USGS.

articles.title: Typhoon Champi kills 1 and injures 350 in Taiwan overnight as storm weakens
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Typhoon Champi killed one person and injured hundreds in Taiwan, as well as downing trees and knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of people as the storm's strong winds and rains continued overnight from Friday into Saturday morning.

Although Champi did not hit Taiwan directly, the storm’s span was large enough to impact most of Taiwan. The island’s weather authorities said the storm was weakening Saturday morning and that by evening, the land warnings for the typhoon would be removed.

Taiwan’s Central Emergency Operations Centre reported that 350 were injured as of Friday night. The one death was a man who was washed away by waves in Taiwan’s Pingtung county, the island’s southernmost part.
Waves generated by Typhoon Champi crash against a seawall in Keelung, Taiwan, on October 23, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

The storm knocked out power for 280,000 households, according to the United Daily News , a local Taiwanese newspaper, citing the island's power authorities. But power had returned to 80% of households by Saturday morning.
Across the island, the storm downed trees and signs, some smaller structures, and even the ceiling of a college dorm in Taipei.

articles.title: Lula, Bolsonaro strike calmer tone in final Brazil election debate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-winger Flavio Bolsonaro held a final, more diplomatic debate on Friday (October 23, 2026), although neither held back with cutting remarks two days before the election.

Polls project a tie between the ideologically opposed pair in Sunday's (October 25, 2026) runoff after Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, took the lead in the first-round vote.

Their first debate was loaded with insults and practically empty of concrete policy proposals, but the candidates this time questioned each other on Brazil's economy, infrastructure and regional development.
There was also a flurry of quips and jibes, with Mr. Lula attacking the 45-year-old senator's lack of experience while Mr. Bolsonaro accused the President of leaving behind a "broken country”.
"He doesn't know what hunger is," Brazil's first working-class president said of Mr. Bolsonaro, who asked the incumbent, "Why are things so expensive?"
The election outcome could see Latin America's largest country join a regional shift to the right championed by U.S. President Donald Trump, or remain a left-wing stronghold.

A Datafolha institute survey published on Thursday (October 22, 2026) showed the pair tied with 50% of voting intentions each, compared to Mr. Bolsonaro's four-point lead in polls published two weeks ago.
Mr. Lula, 80, repeatedly asked viewers to 'Google' Mr. Bolsonaro's claims, to which the senator shot back, "Who governs Brazil, you or Google?"
The right-wing candidate mocked Mr. Lula over the finger he lost in an accident as a metalworker when he was young.
"It's no use, Mr. Lula, giving with one hand and taking away with your nine fingers."
"I will not allow a militiaman to call me 'nine fingers’," Mr. Lula replied, referring to allegations that his rival has ties to paramilitary groups in Rio de Janeiro.
Mr. Bolsonaro apologised, but not without asking Mr. Lula to "apologise to the Brazilian people who suffer from insecurity."

articles.title: As Israeli election nears, campaign turns ugly
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Days ahead of close-fought Israeli elections, campaigns have gone into overdrive with poor-taste jibes and inflammatory attacks against candidates, sometimes crossing red lines.

Fuelled in part by a boom in AI-generated images flooding social media, candidates and activists are seeking to portray their opponents as weak, untrustworthy or damaging for the country as they play on stereotypes and fears to sway public opinion.
The electioneering has at times turned personal, with some candidates who lost loved ones in the wars following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack even having their bereavement dragged into the campaign.
Ahead of Tuesday’s (October 27, 2026) vote , polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc neck and neck with that of his main centre-right rival Gadi Eisenkot.

On Wednesday (October 21, 2026) , Eisenkot posted a video on X wishing Netanyahu a happy 77th birthday that featured a slate of AI-generated characters including a Hamas member speaking from a tunnel.

“What can we wish for the person who has been protecting us for 20 years?” the militant says, evoking theories that the premier has deliberately helped the Islamist movement stay in power in Gaza, charges vehemently denied by Netanyahu.
Soon after, an AI depiction of Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei pops up, telling Netanyahu: “One more round without victory and I’ll make you a bomb as a present.”
Mr. Netanyahu has also liberally weaponised AI-generated content against his rival.
In July, he posted a video depicting Eisenkot rejecting a hug from a young man wearing a T-shirt with the slogan “Israel unity” and instead embracing Arab-Israeli candidate Mansour Abbas.
The clip sparked widespread outrage over claims the young man had been made to resemble Eisenkot’s son who was killed fighting in Gaza in 2023, something Netanyahu’s party denied.
In an interview broadcast by Channel 13, Eisenkot said he had felt “deep contempt for Netanyahu and his entourage” after watching the video.
Mr. Netanyahu’s camp has used AI throughout the campaign to stoke fears over a possible opposition coalition including Arab-Israeli parties.

articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer’s roguelike racing mechanics is not for all
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Ask anyone what the best part of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace is, and every one of them will say the thunderous, high-octane chaos-filled, pod racing sequence. Now, ask anyone what their favourite arcade-style racing game is, and the Burnout series will pretty much be high up on that list.

Burnout was a racing game built around spectacular car crashes, back when burnout meant wrecking cars rather than your mental health. Now, fuse both Episode 1 Racer and Burnout — the chaos, speed and fiddly unpredictability of racing hovering death traps across the galaxy with aggressive vehicular destruction, and you get Star Wars Galactic Racer . Fuse Games, made up of former Burnout developers, has delivered the insanity.

Everyone knows a Kestar Bool in their circles — the spoiled rich kid who makes sure everyone is pushed down so he can succeed. He has been trained by Sebulba (who folks will recognise from The Phantom Menace , as the evil champion of the pod racing circuit), who has passed not only his racing skills to Kestar, but also his nasty ways.

You play as Shade who is tasked with taking down Kestar’s toxic dominance in the Galactic League, a high-stakes illegal racing circuit where many of the top pilots have a place to earn big bucks after the Empire fell. A story that feels quite Star Wars with a healthy dash of Fast and the Furious with aliens, robots and anti-gravity cars.

The game features a Forza Horizon -esque opening sequence that is every bit as cinematic, allowing you to take control of several types of repulsorcraft, which is the fancy sci-fi name for these floating vehicles. The story usually unfolds in quiet walkabout encampment areas where you get to interact with your opponents in a more stationary setting.

It also gives you a chance to speak to various memorable characters, interact with your cute monkey-like mechanic Hibi, and the founder of the League Darius Pax, a mechanic himself and the person who has brought on Shade to help him deal with Kestar. Once you are all storied up, the action then shifts to the high-speed arenas of the Galactic League.

Star Wars Episode 1 Racer was one of the best games of its time when it came out, and it still holds up today. Even if its graphics are dated, the screams, whines and mechanical shivers of those giant engines powering through levels will always be burned in your brain.

There are four distinct types of repulsorcraft you get to scream around corners with — the trusty, souped-up variants of the Landspeeder, which are big, fast moving slabs that look and handle like muscle cars, with a proper drift. Then, there are the speeder bikes, which have absolutely no protection for the rider, but possess a cool kinetic burst-through that swings you out of corners.

The Skim Speeder gives Sony’s Wipeout racing feels with its extended fins and is designed to go very fast, with an ability to tilt vertically to fit through tight gaps. And lastly, there is the return of the Pod Racer, which you only get to pilot in certain events, sadly. Pod Racers are like chariots, but instead of being drawn by horses, they are pulled by massive engines.

These craft absolutely rip through incredible courses. This game is built on aggressive speed and constant danger, and I love how unpredictable the races are. There were moments I was absolutely sure I was going to finish sixth, but after some clever turns and punting a few opponents into oncoming debris, I netted myself a near first. You have to race dirty, pulling off your special moves like forcefields to gain every edge. Managing your boost is key — spit out too much and your craft is going to be panting.
The game introduces a lovely feature called RamJet, which is a secondary-state boost that adds a lot of risk, but if done right you can punch further.

The best part of the whole pod racing sequence is when Anakin’s pod starts malfunctioning, and he has to fiddle with switches to redirect power, fix the kaput engine, then run a very cool-looking, firing up sequence even as the pod is running at a mindblowing speed.

articles.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is a massive improvement over the original
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: This October is turning out to be a case of thanking yourself for holding out on playing certain open world games, starting with the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition which launched on October 1, 2026 with its new expansion that made the game complete. Now it is the turn of 2024’s Dragon Dogma 2; Dark Arisen that not only brings a massive new area, but also fixes quite a lot of the original’s flaws.

Capcom surprising gamers with a sequel to one of their lesser known, but much loved open world RPG’s Dragon’s Dogma, which is now getting a massive expansion, convinces us of the house of Resident Evil ’s motives to make sure all its IPs get the right treatment.

Welcome to Norgon, a cut-off frigid northern land that is harsh, cold and full of unforgiving monsters. At the centre of it all, there is a mysterious new entity known as a Fallen Dragon, that you as an Arisen and your trusty pawns must travel to. Inspired by Norse and Celtic mythology and influences, Norgon may be a smaller region than the main game’s sprawling kingdom, but it has got heights to scale and unknowns lurking in dark ruins.

Guided by a mysterious wanderer Eir, Dark Arisen switches up the political intrigue to a more ancient evil with deeper answers into the dark side of the cosmic cycle that lies at the heart of this world.

But, wait! Norse influence, dragons, cold mountains and ruins, is that you Skyrim? Yes, there is some of that Skyrim vibe to Norgon in there, but it is just atmosphere. The story feels right in Dark Arisen — it is short, focused and has a few memorable characters. Addressing some of the feedback from the original base game, which had a lot of half-baked, Game of Thrones -type stuff happening (read royal conspiracies and political intrigue), Dark Arisen has a strong, fairly linear, mystery at its core. Eir’s role in all this paints quite a picture.
The peeling off those layers to uncover that mystery as you go along is done well, with clear motives laid out for all its strong characters.

One of the strong points of Dragon’s Dogma is in its action system, where you play an Arisen, a being chosen by a dragon by tearing out your heart. This gives you the ability to pull out pawns from a space called the Rift, leaving you a steady source of party members with ready knowledge of other player’s games.

While you have your main pawn as your companion, you can balance your party out with the ones that offset your weaknesses or you can use them as fodder. Dark Arisen pawns however, come with two extra active weapon skills that bump them up from four to six, with skill options. This matters a lot because you do not just craft individual builds, but design complete party wide synergies.

This versatility can let you experiment more while dealing with the fresh monsters and enemies you encounter in this new area. The pawn system, coupled with an excellent fighting system, is what makes Dragon Dogma 2 really sing, especially when you get your builds right. You can now start melting monsters on sight, which was also one of the big problems of the base game.

Norgon functions as a high-level zone, and as a result, you are at the bottom of the food chain again, so you need to grind to get better weapons. This is good because the challenge of facing off and defeating monsters is back. If you have been playing the base game, hitting level 30 automatically puts you into a power fantasy and it can get boring. Monsters now are tougher and you will need to choose the right classes to stand a chance.

Thankfully, there are a lot of side quests and ruins to explore to net relic weapons. Another point of note, there have been multiple patches before Dark Arisen that have massively balanced and optimised the main game, so if you are starting anew, it is not a bad idea. However, it is worth remembering that no amount of patching fixes the main campaign’s insipid slog of a story.

Enemies are tougher, and in the expansion as well, the game seems to regurgitate similar enemy types throughout, though there is some variety, which was one of the big issues of the main game too. But, what the game lacks in variety it makes up for in dropped weapons called relics.

articles.title: Why does Meta have to pay a $25 billion penalty? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Facebook-parent Meta will have to pay $25 billion as a civil penalty for violations of New Mexico’s Unfair Practices Act, announced the U.S. state on October 21. The social media giant was originally slated to pay over $219 billion, or $5,000 per violation found by the jury. However, U.S. Judge Francis Mathew reduced the state penalty to $25 billion, even as the court order observed an “extraordinary number of willful violations” by Meta.

As per the New Mexico Department of Justice (DoJ), the state’s litigation team looked into how Facebook communicated with consumers about its data practices, and the efforts it undertook to tackle misinformation and hate speech.

It found a variety of violations like deceptive statements regarding user privacy and hate speech moderation, unkept commitments on data deletion, poor oversight of developers collecting users’ data, and both public and private misrepresentations of how users could control their Facebook data.

The company’s violations were so numerous that they could not be pinned to a small number of employees, or even attributed to ignorance. On the contrary, the violations were backed by public statements and internal messages by leaders, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

“Rather than seek to educate Facebook’s users about their privacy settings, Mr. Zuckerberg chose instead to capitalize on that lack of understanding in order to manipulate users into sharing more of their personal information publicly; all so that Facebook could better compete with one of its main rivals, Twitter,” stated the court order.

One of the most crucial points in the case is the jury verdict finding that Facebook carried out over 43 million legal violations. The penalty, meanwhile, is meant to reflect the “financial consequences” of Meta’s conduct under the New Mexico law.

For context, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) previously hit Facebook with a $5 billion fine over its post-Cambridge Analytica data practices. The New Mexico civil penalty, which is awarded to the state, is five times that.

Though New Mexico’s lawsuit against Meta stemmed from the Cambridge Analytica data privacy scandal in the 2010s, the legal proceedings expanded to also focus on Meta’s treatment of users’ data between 2010 and 2021.

The $25 billion penalty is the largest fine Meta has ever faced over its conduct. It represents a tremendous — if currently symbolic — victory for a U.S. state that has launched multiple legal challenges against Meta.
In August, a U.S. judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $567 million over child safety lapses on its platforms, adding on to the $375 million the company was ordered to pay this spring.

Now, the eye-watering $25 billion penalty is another achievement for New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez, who has vocally criticised Meta’s operations and child safety record for years. The state sued Meta over its deceptive data handling practices in 2021.

“For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law. A New Mexico jury found nearly 44 million violations of our consumer protection statute, and this penalty order demonstrates that those violations carry real consequences,” said Mr. Torrez in an official statement.

articles.title: Ariel, Umbriel and the man who made them real
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: You know the difference between inventions and discoveries, don’t you? While both of them are fundamental processes that have shaped the course of human history, there’s a difference between them. In simple terms, inventions correspond to coming up with something new based on experimentation and study. Discoveries, meanwhile, are the process of finding something that already exists, especially for the first time.

When we speak of Ariel and Umbriel, two of Uranus’ many moons (29 officially as of August 2026), it is their discovery that we talk about. This is because these satellites have existed for a very long time, and it was only their existence that was revealed in reality when English astronomer William Lassell discovered them.

Born in Bolton, England on June 18, 1799, Lassell belonged to a family that was fairly well-off. The boy born close to the turn of the century turned into a teen who moved from Rochdale, Manchester to Toxteth, Liverpool in 1815. Here, he apprenticed in a local merchant’s office until 1822. His life was just about to hit the fast-forward button.

He set out as a beer brewer on Milton Street in Liverpool by November 1824 and business soon flourished. Riches led him to leisure, leisure lent him time, and time turned into newfound interests. Astronomy turned out to be the unexpected beneficiary due to the wealth that he accumulated.
Portrait of William Lassell. | Photo Credit: Wikimedia Commons

He made so much money that he was able to build an observatory at his own home! By the summer of 1839, ‘Starfield’ on West Derby Road was established with a 9-inch diameter telescope that Lassell built on his own. This only served to whet his appetite and he paid a visit to Irish engineer and astronomer William Parsons, 3ʳᵈ Earl Rosse. Lord Rosse was the designer of the Leviathan of Parsonstown, the largest telescope of the time — a record it held into the next century.

Returning to Liverpool with more knowledge of the subject, Lassell went on to build a successful partnership with two others. Fellow English amateur astronomer William Rutter Dawes also had his own observatory in Ormskirk, and he had a keen eye for testing calibrating telescopes. James Nasmyth, a Scottish engineer and the inventor of the steam hammer, turned to astronomy following retirement from business as a mechanical engineer. All three of them — Lassell, Dawes, and Nasmyth — were recognised as the “Grand Amateurs” of astronomy.

The trio built a telescope with a diameter of 24 inches that was constructed in Lassell’s workshops at Starfield. The 20-foot-long tube with a mirror that ran two feet across was polished using a machine of Lassell’s own design and was the first telescope of its size to achieve equatorial mounting. This enabled them to not only track down specific objects, but also observe and follow them for a longer period. The discoveries were just around the corner.

In a period of five years, Lassell discovered four satellites in the solar system using this telescope. The first of these discoveries took place on October 10, 1846, when Lassell discovered Triton. The largest of Neptune’s satellites was discovered by Lassell just 17 days after Neptune itself had been discovered! If Neptune were the size of a basketball, then Triton would be as small as a bead that is one-and-a-half centimetres across — an indicator of how good Lassell’s telescope was.
This image taken by Voyager 2 in 1986 shows Umbriel, one of the two moons of Uranus that Lassell discovered. | Photo Credit: NASA / Wikimedia Commons

In 1848, Lassell discovered Hyperion, the largest of Saturn’s irregular, non-spherical moons. Lassell shares this discovery with William Cranch Bond and his son George Phillips Bond — an American father-son duo who independently discovered the same moon.

On October 24, 1851, Lassell doubled the number of satellites he had discovered from two to four. Using the same telescope that had yielded success, Lassell discovered Ariel and Umbriel. The discovery of these two new moons of Uranus added to the two moons (Titania and Oberon in 1787) that had already been discovered shortly after the planet itself had been discovered in 1781.

articles.title: The other face of air pollution | Excerpt from The Nitrogen Bomb by Jacob Koshy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) stretches across northern India in a 2,500-kilometre arc from Pakistan to Bangladesh and is home to nearly half a billion people. It is one of the most intensively farmed landscapes on earth, and by every atmospheric measure, one of the most chemically burdened places that has been peopled for millennia. What Odén [Svante Odén, the Swedish scientist who first linked acid rain and its wide-ranging environmental harms] mapped in Scandinavia — nitrogen from farms, nitrogen oxides from engines, ammonia reacting with acids to produce particles that choke lungs and kill quietly — is happening here, now, on a scale and at a speed that would make Europe’s post-war industrial peak antediluvian.

In 2025, I reported on a study by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a think tank, that said secondary pollutants, particularly ammonium sulphate that forms when sulphur dioxide from coal plants meets ammonia from fertilised fields, were responsible for nearly one-third of India’s PM2.5 pollution burden.

I remember writing then, trying to explain to readers who, like me, had been led to believe that Delhi’s winters were a problem of primary pollutants from stubble fires and diesel exhaust: ‘Primary pollutants are those that result from the burning of fossil fuels from automobiles, coal plants and organic matter.’ The distinction matters because it changes everything about how you think about solutions. During Delhi’s most polluted winter months, the CREA analysis found, it was secondary pollutants that constituted nearly 41 per cent of all fine particles in the winter air. The problem isn’t what you can see coming out of a tailpipe or a chimney but what is being silently assembled in the atmosphere, molecule by molecule and reaction by reaction.

The one-third figure, however, carries a chemist’s caveat. Professor Srinidhi Balasubramanian, who teaches in the Department of Environmental Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, has spent close to two decades studying ammonia as an agricultural air pollutant — first in the maize belt of the American Midwest, at the University of Illinois, following it up at the University of Minnesota, and now across the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

She begins her air-quality exposition to me with a line borrowed from a Class VII science textbook. ‘Acid plus base forms a salt,’ she told me. ‘It is as simple as that.’ The acids are the familiar villains — nitrogen oxides from combustion and the sulphur dioxide from coal that is yellowing the Taj Mahal. The base, ‘the single most dominant one, by any stretch’, is ammonia, and the source of that ammonia is overwhelmingly agricultural. Her 2021 work put the farming share at roughly 80 per cent globally, and India, she reckons, at 80 to 85 per cent, the rest leaking from fertiliser plants and industry.

If you look at it, it is the other side of the coin that Odén puzzled over in Scandinavia. The problem he had identified was acids and what she is drawing attention to is the base. ‘This is the other face of acid rain,’ Balasubramanian said. ‘As acid rain reduces, your PM problem exaggerates.’ Where Smith’s Manchester and Odén’s Sweden carried a surplus of acid and watched it fall, the fertilised plains of northern India carry, on top of their acids, an overwhelming surplus of the base — and the salt the two make is settling into human lungs. Her own modelling refines the arithmetic behind the CREA figure: ammonia acting alone accounts for about a quarter of India’s PM2.5, she estimates; bundled with the nitrogen oxides and coal-derived sulphur it reacts with, the inorganic secondary fraction climbs to roughly 40 per cent, and with the organic secondaries added, the national balance tips to something like 45 per cent primary against 55 per cent secondary.

Dr. Balasubramanian is among the small group of Indian scientists who have been tracing the chemistry of what happens over the IGP, across multiple institutions. The foundational work began at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur (IIT-K) with Sachchida Nand Tripathi, who in 2003 established what would become the National Aerosol Facility, the first of its kind in India.

Kanpur is almost the geographic centre of the IGP and from here his group built the long-term datasets on trace gases and aerosol properties that first revealed the seasonal patterns of IGP pollution. A 2014 study from his lab documented four years of continuous measurements of SO2, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and ozone at Kanpur, establishing the winter loading patterns that make IGP winters chemically unlike any other season anywhere. Cold temperatures push the chemical equilibrium towards the particle phase, and the planetary boundary layer — the lid of air above the city — often compresses below 400 metres, trapping precursor gases until they react. Nitrogen oxides from vehicles and industry peak in winter, the group found, at exactly the moment when the atmospheric conditions for converting them to ammonium nitrate particles are most favourable.

articles.title: New form of carbon found: diamondiyne
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon
(This article forms a part of the Science for All newsletter that takes the jargon out of science and puts the fun in! Subscribe now! )
Scientists have created a new form of carbon called diamondiyne. It is a three-dimensional network of carbon atoms that resembles a diamond but with a more open structure.
Researchers first proposed the existence of this form more than three decades ago and it has finally been synthesised. The findings were reported in the journal Angewandte Chemie .

Carbon atoms can bond together to form crystals of different shapes, called allotropes. The three most famous ones are graphite, diamond, and graphene. While in diamond each carbon atom bonds to four neighbours, in the graphene the atoms form a flat sheet. Diamondiyne is more akin to diamond but it more closely resembles two open jungle gyms — the grid of cages you see in parks where children can climb and swing from — pushed through each other, with more spacious cages, with more room within the structure than diamonds.

Scientists took so long to create this allotrope because one of its chemical building blocks is unstable and because if the bonds do not connect properly in the process of making it, they can be difficult to undo.

The researchers who succeeded, from the University of Gothenburg, Stock University, and the Chalmers University of Technology, all in Sweden, did so by making the material at a boundary between water and chloroform, with the chemical reaction slowly releasing the building blocks and allowing them to link up at a rate the team could control. (The ‘y’ in the material’s name comes from the presence of carbon-carbon triple bonds.)

The process — which could take around a week — produced thin films of carbon covering around five square centimetres each. The researchers could control their thickness by slowing down or speeding up the reaction, from a few nanometres to up to 60 nanometres.
The team used spectroscopy and electron microscopy to confirm the films contained small diamondiyne crystals. However, it was present only to the tune of 1% of the reaction yield.
Scientists often pursue research like this in order to discover what forms matter can take and how the ways in which their atoms are arranged control their properties as a material.

Carbon in particular poses an interesting case because while diamond is extremely hard and an electrical insulator, graphite is soft and conducts electricity, yet both are allotropes of the same element. By extension, synthesising the new allotrope has reinforced the notion that scientists can potentially create materials with radically different properties but without changing their chemical composition.
And some discoveries could eventually lead to a material that might be useful in electronics, storing energy or some other technology that the world is looking for.

articles.title: Falling short: on Marco Rubio’s second visit to India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The United States Secretary of State’s three-day visit to India , his second in five months, came at a significant time in U.S. politics. Marco Rubio’s Mumbai trip this week was just ahead of the U.S. midterm elections , which would mark the midpoint of President Donald Trump’s second term in office — a point at which the incumbent normally begins to focus on legacy, and possible contenders for the next Presidential election (Mr. Rubio is expected to be one), and start to look for possible partners and friendships around the world. In addition, his visit also raised hopes in New Delhi of a reset in bilateral ties, battered by two years of uncertainty over the Trump administration’s actions. This would include positive moves towards concluding the Bilateral Trade Agreement , reassuring India about U.S. sanctions on the import of Russian oil, preparations for upcoming Trump meets with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Manila (ASEAN) and Miami (G-20) summits, discussing plans for the Quad Summit (on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit) that India has been trying to host, and setting a date for Mr. Trump’s India visit. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s invitation also offered Mr. Rubio an opportunity to meet their UAE counterpart, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to discuss the Gulf situation and to restore energy security and connectivity. And finally, Mr. Rubio’s visit to the Jamnagar Reliance refinery, led to speculation of some major deals on energy, possibly offering more discounts as he pitched for India to buy more American and U.S.-licensed Venezuelan oil.

Given all the high expectations, the visit was bound to come up short. The optics of his visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar, but not New Delhi, which was announced by the U.S. Ambassador to India , gave the Opposition fodder to question the real purpose of the visit. Despite Mr. Rubio’s two visits to India and more than six by Mr. Jaishankar to the U.S. since Mr. Trump took office, relations remain on edge, with issues on trade, tariffs, H-1B restrictions and anti-immigrant measures unaddressed. Also, the U.S.’s narrative on Operation Sindoor (2025), growing ties with Pakistan, and the Trump administration’s rhetoric on India’s economy, diaspora and Russian oil trade have added to India’s unhappiness. The two sides did not announce any agreements and Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Rubio did not hold a joint press address. However, as they did at the U.S. Independence Day’s 250th anniversary celebrations in Delhi in May, they attended the “Freedom 250” event in Mumbai. Mr. Rubio acknowledged that while no two countries would agree on all issues, he said the U.S.-India alignment on core issues of national interest was “extraordinary” . From this point on, Mr. Rubio must walk that talk, with a view to ensuring that India-U.S. ties are able to move on from the difficulties of the last few years.

articles.title: In the crossfire: on India and the Saudi-Houthi conflict
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The killing of an Indian national in a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Dammam airport is a grim reminder of the dangers the kingdom’s Indian community faces as the conflict between Riyadh and Yemen’s Shia militants escalates. Since the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis resumed in July, at least two Indians have been killed and 14 others wounded. On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that a yacht with 14 Indians was targeted by Saudi forces near Yemen’s Zuqar island in the Red Sea and that rescue operations were under way. As the Houthis, who control parts of Northern Yemen and its entire Red Sea coast, step up attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including oil facilities and airports, Indians, who are the kingdom’s largest expat community, risk getting caught in the crossfire. With flights disrupted, thousands of Indian pilgrims are stranded. India has condemned Houthi attacks, saying that it “stands in solidarity” with Saudi Arabia. With no end in sight to the fighting and a high possibility of Israel and the U.S. resuming their Iran strikes, further violence and instability in West Asia could make India’s choices increasingly difficult.

The Saudi-Houthi conflict dates back to the Houthi takeover of Sana’a, Yemen’s capital, in 2014. A year later, Saudi Arabia began bombing Yemen to drive the Houthis out. But years of Saudi bombing of one of the poorest Arab countries have proved counterproductive; the Houthis consolidated support among the tribes of northern Yemen and built a powerful territorial army and naval force. The Saudi-Houthi ceasefire of 2022 collapsed in July 2026 after Saudi Arabia recklessly bombed Sana’a airport, to prevent an Iranian plane with a Houthi delegation from landing. The Houthis subsequently began attacking Saudi Arabia’s critical infrastructure, and launched a ground offensive against the Saudi-backed forces in Yemen. The Houthi attacks pose the biggest security challenge to Mohammed bin Salman, Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince and the main architect of the war on Yemen, in decades. Massive Saudi air strikes have neither defeated the Houthis nor restored the kingdom’s deterrence. With its wealth, natural resources, infrastructure and tenuous palace politics, the kingdom remains exposed to Houthi missile and drone attacks, with few good options for a way out. India must prepare a contingency plan for worst-case scenarios. Its immediate priority should be to evacuate stranded Indian pilgrims. It should also articulate a stronger position for stability and work with Arab countries and Tehran to push for a diplomatic settlement to the Iran crisis . For peace to prevail in the Persian Gulf, the guns directed at Iran must first fall silent.

articles.title: Canary in the coal mine: On the performance of India’s core industrial sectors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The latest data on the performance of the core industrial sectors show the economy may be facing an industrial uptick, but questions about its sustainability remain. Growth in the Index of Core Industries rose to a series-high of 7.9% in September 2026, the second consecutive month of accelerated performance. Any such improvement is to be celebrated, but a deeper look at what is driving it is also warranted. The coal sector saw growth suddenly shoot up to 10.7% in September. The unexpected and unusual nature of this rapid acceleration can be borne out by the fact that the sector contracted by 1.1% over the longer April-September 2026 period. The growth in coal in September was likely a temporary blip aided by a statistical low base and, more importantly, pressure from power plant operators over rapidly depleting coal stocks amid the heat wave. The electricity sector grew 11.4% in September, capping off a half-year dominated by double-digit growth. This surge in electricity-related demand for coal will likely wane, especially since the El Niño factor that drove the heat wave will also result in a milder winter. The other sector that results in high coal usage, the steel sector, did accelerate in September, but not by enough to sustain the coal sector’s September output. The uptick in steel did, however, result in a return to double-digit growth for the iron ore sector, which should bode well for the mining component of the larger Index of Industrial Production.

The performance of the crude oil, natural gas, and refinery products sectors also highlights the fiscal problems India faces. At a time when the crude oil and natural gas sectors have both contracted continuously since 2024, refinery output rose to 10.3% in September. This means that the refineries were increasingly processing expensive imported oil. India’s oil imports in September were up 7% by volume but jumped 47% in terms of value due to the high price of oil. This is set to worsen. The attacks on Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure have already pushed global oil prices above $112 a barrel, almost a six-month high. The reprieve from the U.S. on potential tariffs linked to imports of Russian oil provide India a reliable source, but the days of discounts are long gone. It is the time of premium pricing, and each barrel imported is eating into India’s foreign exchange reserves, which are also being used to defend the rupee. Cement and steel are the only sustainably growing core sectors, and those too are based on government infrastructure spending. At a time when industrial output is only temporarily propped up, the government’s fiscal space is fast shrinking.

articles.title: Tunnelling through: On China’s export control list, tunnel-boring machines
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs decision to place tunnel-boring machines (TBMs) on an export control list reveals a blind spot in India’s supply chain diversification. The curbs include TBMs, walking excavators, and high-altitude wet shotcrete machines. From November 18, if a shipment is intended for countries or regions deemed sensitive due to ongoing disputes with China, exporters will need an export licence from commerce authorities. For other countries/regions, exporters will need to be registered, obtain an export certificate, and submit end-use declarations stating that the equipment will not be re-routed to sensitive locations. While China has cornered around 70% of the global TBM market, prominent manufacturers in the West also maintain substantial component supply chains in the country to cut manufacturing overhead. Further, TBMs are complex to build as they have to be configured to geological characteristics at the project site and perform numerous tasks. Where a suitable TBM exists, it can be used for civilian or military purposes. India has struggled with TBM-related hold-ups with China for at least two years now, including for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail project. Germany’s Herrenknecht AG set up an assembling and refurbishing facility in Chennai in 2007-08. TBM production economics differ significantly from conventional construction equipment as new plants need a minimum number of orders and must be able to access the industrial capability required to design, manufacture and repair specialised components.

However, even though India is one of the world’s largest TBM importers, expecting every sophisticated machine to be produced domestically will send public infrastructure costs soaring. Even now, depending on China’s decision on the TBMs set for India, India may have to redirect its procurement to facilities based directly in Germany or Japan, say, and absorb the higher capital cost. The BEML experience shows that manufacturing partnerships can fail without secure licensing arrangements and access to sustained demand. India should pursue domestic manufacturing alongside international partnerships, e.g., making equipment in the country under agreement with established foreign firms, and develop shared industrial capabilities rather than singular ‘national champions’, as TBM manufacturers and their suppliers can benefit from access to common testing and precision manufacturing infrastructure. Overall, Beijing is systematically identifying sectors where it commands a significant global capacity and establishing export controls to counter western technological restrictions, such as on advanced semiconductors, so any critical infrastructure sector relying on Chinese supply lines will face a compounding geopolitical risk.
